minutes.headline: Selectmen declined to second a motion to put five marijuana prohibition questions on the May 2019 ballot.
minutes.summary: A joint meeting with the Planning Board debated putting five separate marijuana-establishment prohibition questions and a regulation article before voters. A motion to add them to the May 2019 ballot got no second, and the chair wanted to wait for a full board. A second joint meeting with the Parks Commission discussed the size, parking, maintenance and location of a proposed skate park, with no decision.

what_happened.line: A motion to put the Planning Board's marijuana prohibition questions on the May 2019 ballot failed for lack of a second.
The chair said the marijuana item would return when the full board is present, with the January 8 meeting committed to discussion of marijuana.
In a joint meeting with the Parks Commission, the board discussed the skate park's size, parking, maintenance and location; no decision was made.
The skate park group is to return with questions and talk with the Senior Center, and a smaller, phased design is to be explored.
A January 15 workshop on town facilities was planned; the next meeting is December 18.

why_it_matters: Whether marijuana establishments are prohibited in town is a question voters may be asked at the ballot, and the board's delay leaves the May 2019 ballot content undecided.
A skate park would use town land and money for building and upkeep, and its cost grew as the design grew, so a smaller, phased plan could change what the town is asked to pay.
watch_next: January 8 meeting: discussion of the marijuana ballot questions with the full board present.
January 15 workshop on town facilities; next regular meeting December 18.
